title: Invariant reduced projective closures and boundary ideals
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space with a rational representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace, def-sc-general-linear-group]. Put $\mathbf P(V)=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, where in a basis $S=k[z_0,\ldots,z_{\dim V-1}]$ is the total-degree graded polynomial ring [def-pc-proj, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; use the induced action on the space of lines. Let $W\subseteq\mathbf P(V)$ be a reduced locally closed subscheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion] invariant in the scheme sense that the projective action restricts to $G\times_k W\to W$. Let $Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|W|}$, and $B$ the reduced induced closed subscheme on $|Z|\setminus |W|$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Then $W$ identifies with the open subscheme $Z\setminus |B|$, and $Z$ and $B$ are invariant closed subschemes of $\mathbf P(V)$: their restricted actions exist and all inclusions are equivariant. For $C=Z$ or $C=B$ and $d\geq0$, let $I(C)_d\subseteq S_d$ be the space of degree-$d$ polynomials whose section restricts to zero on $C$, equivalently those for which every $f/z_i^d$ restricts to zero on $C\cap D_+(z_i)$. Then $I(C)_d$ is a finite-dimensional rational $G$-subrepresentation of $S_d$ for the contragredient polynomial action $(g\cdot f)(v)=f(\rho(g)^{-1}v)$. Explicitly the action on $S_d\otimes_k A$ preserves $I(C)_d\otimes_k A$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $g\in G(A)$, and restricts to a group-scheme representation on $I(C)_d$. Empty $W$, empty boundary, disconnected $G$, and all characteristics are permitted; smoothness of $G$ is retained.

source.place: Agent-formulated scheme-level closure and boundary-ideal input to Section 7e (linear actions) and Lemma 13.46. Section 1, Corollary 1.18, determination of reduced closed subvarieties by geometric points; Section 4, representations and subrepresentations. Homogeneous ideal interface: Stacks Tag 03GL, constructions.tex, lemma-closed-in-projective-space. This equivariant combination is not quoted as a theorem of Milne or of Tag 03GL.

proof.text: Choose an open subscheme $U\subseteq\mathbf P(V)$ in which $W$ is closed, as in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Closure commutes with restriction to an open subset, so $\overline{|W|}\cap U=|W|$. Both $W$ and $Z\cap U$ are reduced closed subschemes of $U$: restrictions of the reduced structure sheaf remain reduced. Their supports coincide; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies them over $U$. Thus $W$ is the open subscheme $Z\cap U$ of $Z$, and its complement $|B|$ is closed in $Z$ and in $\mathbf P(V)$, because $Z$ is closed there. The same uniqueness constructs the reduced boundary $B$ in $Z$. Its inclusion in $\mathbf P(V)$ is closed: on an affine ambient chart the two closed inclusions correspond to $R\twoheadrightarrow R/I\twoheadrightarrow (R/I)/J$, whose composite is the quotient by the inverse image of $J$. In particular $W=Z\setminus|B|$ as schemes, not merely as sets.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness; Remark 0F2L, remark-reduced-induced-locally-closed (open restriction).

proof.text: For $g\in G(k)$, let $a_g$ be its projective automorphism; its inverse is $a_{g^{-1}}$ by the action identities. The assumed restricted action on $W$ gives $a_g(|W|)=|W|$, using $g^{-1}$ for the reverse inclusion. A homeomorphism preserves closure, so $a_g(|Z|)=|Z|$; subtracting $|W|$ gives $a_g(|B|)=|B|$. Transporting a reduced closed subscheme through an automorphism gives another reduced closed subscheme with the transported support. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] therefore gives $a_g(Z)=Z$ and $a_g(B)=B$ as closed subschemes. This argument uses each individual $g$, with no connectedness assumption.

source.place: Corollary 1.18, printed p.11; agent application of reduced-induced uniqueness to projective automorphisms.

proof.text: Fix $C=Z$ or $B$. Smoothness gives that $G$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to the fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The standard affine charts of $C$ are quotients of $k[z_j/z_i:j\ne i]$ by ideals, by [def-pc-proj] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]; their rings are reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. They are finitely generated. Choose an affine cover of $G$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then [lem-wf-affine-product-reduced] gives an affine cover of $G\times_k C$ by reduced finitely generated $k$-algebras. Its $k$-points are pairs $(g,c)$. Those points are dense on each such chart: if a nonempty principal open $D(h)$ contained no $k$-point, $h$ would vanish at every $k$-point and hence be zero by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing], contradicting nonemptiness. Principal opens form a basis in an affine spectrum. Thus $G\times_k C$ is reduced and its $k$-points are topologically dense.

source.place: Propositions 1.10--1.12, printed pp.9--10; Stacks Tag 056T, varieties.tex lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; product input as stated in lem-wf-affine-product-reduced.

proof.text: The inverse image of the closed subset $|C|$ under $a:G\times_k C\to\mathbf P(V)$ is closed and contains every $k$-point by step 2. Density from step 3 makes this inverse image all of $G\times_k C$. Since that source is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $a$ through $C$. This is the required morphism $a_C:G\times_k C\to C$. Its unit and associativity identities follow by composing both sides with $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V)$ and using the ambient action identities. Such composition detects equality: on affine target charts, the defining ring homomorphism is surjective, so two factorizations through the quotient agreeing before factorization agree. The same uniqueness proves equivariance of $B\hookrightarrow Z$, $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V)$, and the open inclusion $W\hookrightarrow Z$. Hence these are scheme actions, not just actions of $G(k)$.

source.place: Tag 0356, lemma-map-into-reduction; uniqueness of factorization through an affine quotient, as in Definition 01IO.

proof.text: The degree-$d$ monomials $z^\alpha$ with $\sum_i\alpha_i=d$ form a basis of $S_d$ by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; their index set is finite since $0\leq\alpha_i\leq d$. For every $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, substitute the linear forms given by $\rho_A(g)^{-1}$ for the variables in $A[z_0,\ldots,z_{\dim V-1}]$. The polynomial universal property gives an $A$-linear automorphism $r_{d,A}(g)$ of the homogeneous degree-$d$ part $S_d\otimes_k A$. Its inverse substitutes $\rho_A(g)$. Substitution commutes with homomorphisms $A\to A'$. Moreover $r_{d,A}(g)r_{d,A}(h)f(v)=f(\rho_A(h)^{-1}\rho_A(g)^{-1}v)=f(\rho_A(gh)^{-1}v)$; the identity matrix acts identically. Thus these are natural group representations. The finite-dimensional clause of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] makes them a group-scheme representation on $S_d$. This is precisely the required contragredient polynomial action.

source.place: Remark 4.1, printed p.84, and Section 7f, printed p.145, dual and symmetric-power action; explicit substitution inserts inversion to obtain a left action.

proof.text: For $C=Z$ or $B$, the spaces $I(C)_d$ are the chart-vanishing degree pieces in [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal], applied with $n=\dim V-1\geq0$. In particular they are linear subspaces of the finite-dimensional space $S_d$. On each reduced affine chart $C\cap D_+(z_i)$, [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] says that $f/z_i^d$ is zero if and only if it is zero at all $k$-points of that chart. Consequently $f\in I(C)_d$ if and only if $f(v)=0$ for every nonzero vector $v\in V$ whose line $[v]$ is in $C(k)$: choose $i$ with $v_i\ne0$ and use $(f/z_i^d)([v])=f(v)/v_i^d$. For $g\in G(k)$ step 2 puts $[\rho(g)^{-1}v]$ in $C(k)$ whenever $[v]\in C(k)$. Hence $r_{d,k}(g)f$ satisfies the same vanishing criterion. Applying this also to $g^{-1}$ proves $r_{d,k}(g)I(C)_d=I(C)_d$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, definition of I_d; Milne Corollary 1.18 and the affine vanishing principle, applied in the standard trivializations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-rational-point-subspace-test] to the rational representation $r_d$ constructed in step 5 and its subspace $I(C)_d$, stable on $G(k)$ by step 6. Its hypotheses hold: $k$ is algebraically closed, $G$ is smooth affine of finite type, and $S_d$ is finite-dimensional. Its conclusion gives $r_{d,A}(g)(I(C)_d\otimes_k A)=I(C)_d\otimes_k A$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $g\in G(A)$. Restrict these automorphisms to that submodule; their inverses, group identities and naturality restrict as well. Choosing a basis of $I(C)_d$ and extending it to one of $S_d$ identifies its tensor with the corresponding direct summand after any scalar extension, so the restrictions are natural automorphisms of $(I(C)_d)_A$. The finite-dimensional clause of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] now gives a group-scheme representation on $I(C)_d$, and its inclusion intertwines the actions. This proves rational subrepresentation, including stability over nonreduced algebras $A$.

source.place: Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85; Remark 4.1, printed p.84, for the natural restricted representation.

proof.text: If $W=\varnothing$, its closure and boundary are empty and the degree pieces are all $S_d$; if $B=\varnothing$, its pieces are likewise $S_d$. For nonempty $C$, $I(C)_0=0$, since a nonzero constant cannot vanish on a nonempty chart; the zero subspace has the unique trivial representation. When $\dim V=1$, projective space has its single standard chart and the same arguments apply. No step divides by a positive integer, uses connectedness of $G$, or assumes that $A$ is reduced. Smoothness is used to make $G$ reduced and to invoke the rational-point subspace test. These observations verify all the stated degenerate cases.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-e2ac83993 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 steps and the 14 cited statements in full. The delivery adds no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged; the only stmt_deps change adds def-weil-module-base-change, which the statement needs for the tensor clause. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, and there is no repair note. Step by step: (1) W is closed in an open U, the closure meets U in |W|, and uniqueness of the reduced induced structure (01J3, 0F2L) gives W = Z\|B| as schemes; B -> P(V) is closed as a composite of quotients. (2) a_g is a homeomorphism, so it preserves Z and B as reduced subschemes by uniqueness; this works for each g separately (cf. Milne Cor 1.18). (3) G is reduced by sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced applied to the fibre over k; the charts of C are reduced and finitely generated; lem-wf-affine-product-reduced applies; density of k-points follows from the Nullstellensatz vanishing clause. (4) The factorization lemma applies because the source is reduced; the action identities and equivariance follow because closed immersions are monomorphisms. (5) The action by substituting rho(g)^{-1} is a left action, (gh)^{-1}=h^{-1}g^{-1}, matching Milne 7f p.145 (checked; 7e->7f correction right); the dictionary's finite-dimensional clause makes it a homomorphism to GL. (6) I(C)_d equals the 03GL-node I_d; vanishing on k-points gives G(k)-stability, both inclusions. (7) The hypotheses of the subspace test hold exactly (Milne Cor 4.4-4.5); direction (i)=>(ii) covers every algebra A including nonreduced ones; restricting via a basis extension and the dictionary gives the subrepresentation. (8) The edge cases are right: empty C, I_0, dim V=1, every characteristic. I tested a small case: G_m with weights (0,1) on k^2 gives I(B)_d spanned by z0^a z1^b with a,b>=1, which is a subrepresentation. The five off-unit tool_uses are generic black boxes and are accepted. Stacks tags 01J3, 0F2L, 0356, 03GL and 056T are verified; no SGA source is used, and the DAG search found no duplicate.
